text:
sam: grabbed a short Nsight/GPU trace from the job that regressed yesterday. timeline shows repeated ring idle gaps when we switch kernels during kv-merge -> attention precompute. here's a link to the capture: https://internal-nsight/reports/1799004321 (screenshot in thread).

anya: hmm does this line up with the kernel-selector change we pushed last week? the one that heuristically prefers fused_matmul_v2 for seq>1024?

sam: yes, rollout started on Friday. the odd bit is that only partition 2/8 shows the long tail. others are fine. nvprof-ish summary: allreduce tail ~8-12ms on p2, while baseline was ~2-3ms. aggregate compute time didn't increase proportionally. smells like comm/compute overlap lost.

jordan: can you paste the custom-timer dump? the small timers we added around kv-prefetch,kernel-switch,allreduce would help.

sam: pasted below (converted to quick CSV):
``` 
device,marker,wall_ms
p0,kv_prefetch_start,0.0
p0,kv_prefetch_end,1.2
p0,kernel_launch,1.4
p0,allreduce_start,2.8
p0,allreduce_end,5.2
p1,kv_prefetch_start,0.0
p1,kv_prefetch_end,1.1
p1,kernel_launch,1.3
p1,allreduce_start,6.0
p1,allreduce_end,18.0
```

sam: see p1 allreduce_end huge tail. device skew causes other ranks to spin-wait.

devon: what changed in kernel selector? I recall it tries to avoid a copy for quantized matmuls by selecting a slower but memory-friendlier kernel when batch<8. maybe we introduced a path that serializes an async memcpy -> sync kernel launch on some inputs.

mike: two quick checks: 1) run with REDWOOD_KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy to see if it reverts. 2) set REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=0 to disable prefetch path and check overlap. both cheap.

sam: i ran the legacy selector on the same workload, allreduce tails drop to ~3ms and overall latency matches baseline. set of runs with prefetch toggled: with prefetch on, tails present; prefetch off, tails much smaller. win points to kv-prefetch<->kernel handoff timing.

anya: could prefetch be blocking the stream used for comms? if prefetch uses same stream and causes a sync point at kernel-switch, then NCCL ops might be forced to wait.

jordan: cc @devon can you audit the stream assignment in the new selector? look for `cudaStreamSynchronize` or uses of default stream in the prefetchnative path. also check whether we accidentally introduced a `cudaDeviceSynchronize` for error checking in the hot path.

devon: will check. preliminary grep shows `if (use_prefetch) cudaMemcpyAsync(..., stream);` then later a `launch_kernel(...);` with stream passed, but i found one spot using `CHECK_CUDA_CALL(cudaGetLastError())` without stream query — might be turning implicit sync on some architectures.

sam: attached a mini-reproducer in the thread (run on 8gpus w/ 2 microbatches): `./bin/kv_prefetch_probe --batch 2 --seq 2048 --selector fused_v2`

mike: can we add a lightweight timer on the NCCL ops to confirm whether NCCL is actually waiting or the kernel finishes late? small changes: add `ncclCommUserStream` probe and sample `ncclAllReduce` start/end timestamps from host wall.

sam: did that. host-space NCCL start shows requests issued early, but host-side end reported later on p1. combined with device timers suggests p1 kernel launch is delayed (or its launch callback blocks).

ci-bot: perf/run-1799004321 finished: 6/6 runs passed smoke, but regression delta +12% p99 latency for that config. See CI link: https://ci.internal/runs/1799004321

anya: next steps: 1) devon to remove suspicious error-checking calls and push a patch to avoid implicit sync. 2) mike to add NCCL per-rank timers and a short nsight capture with the legacy and new selector for comparison. 3) sam to extend reproducer to vary microbatch counts to see sensitivity.

jordan: also create a perf regression ticket and tag it `perf:regression,eng-runtime` and attach the nsight capture + timer CSVs. assign to devon, priority P1 for Dedicated customers.

devon: ack. i'll run through the code and post a tiny PR that changes the error-check path to `cudaGetLastError` only in debug builds and replaces the production check with cudaPeekAtLastError() or stream-specified checks.

sam: thanks. i'd like to re-run 3x with the fix and collect nsight traces. if that reduces tail we're good to roll back the selector change for canary.

mike: also note: batching heuristics might interact — if fused_v2 reduces per-invocation time, batching windows shrink and KV prefetch timing shifts. we should run with both small and large microbatch knobs.

anya: good catch. keep the reproducer params in the ticket.

sam: one more note — saw one weird GC on host process around the time of tails, maybe python gc in orchestrator paused RPC and delayed NCCL launch on that rank. low prob but capture during CI would rule it out.

jordan: okay, looks actionable. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
